name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Metrolina
description: Regional food bank supplying partner pantries and meal programs across 24 counties in North and South Carolina.
hours: Mon-Fri, 7:30 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Food is distributed through partner agencies. Use the online agency finder or call to locate a nearby pantry.
source: Second Harvest Food Bank of Metrolina website

name: Nourish Up
description: Formerly Loaves & Fishes and Friendship Trays, providing groceries, meal delivery, and medically tailored meals in Charlotte.
hours: Call for pantry and meal-delivery schedules
eligibility: Serves older adults and people with medical needs. Call to check eligibility for groceries or meal delivery.

name: Roof Above
description: Day services, emergency shelter, and housing programs for people experiencing homelessness in Mecklenburg County.
hours: Day Services Center Mon-Fri; coordinated entry sign-ups at 8:30 AM and 1:30 PM
eligibility: Adults experiencing homelessness or housing instability. Call 704-284-9665 for a coordinated entry assessment.

name: Charlotte Family Housing
description: Shelter and rapid-rehousing programs that help families move from homelessness to stable, permanent housing.
hours: Call for intake and office hours
eligibility: Families experiencing homelessness in Mecklenburg County. Intake is completed by phone or online interest form.

name: Crisis Assistance Ministry
description: Emergency rent and utility assistance, a free store, and case management for Mecklenburg County residents.
hours: Financial assistance lobby Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-4:00 PM; Free Store Tue-Sat, 10:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents with a short-term financial emergency and a regular source of household income. Documents required.

name: Safe Alliance
description: Confidential crisis support, shelter, counseling, and court advocacy for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.
hours: Greater Charlotte Hope Line available 24/7; administrative office Mon-Fri
eligibility: Free and confidential services for people affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking.

name: The Relatives
description: Youth crisis shelter, crisis hotline, and drop-in services for young people who are homeless, displaced, or in crisis.
hours: Youth Crisis Center open 24/7; On Ramp Resource Center Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: Youth ages 7-17 for crisis shelter; young adults ages 16-24 for On Ramp drop-in services.

name: Charlotte Rescue Mission
description: Free residential recovery programs for men and women facing homelessness and substance use disorders.
hours: Call for intake and program availability
eligibility: Adults seeking recovery from substance use. Call for intake screening and program requirements.

name: NC MedAssist
description: Statewide free pharmacy and prescription assistance for North Carolina residents who cannot afford medications.
address: 4428 Taggart Creek Road, Suite 101, Charlotte, NC 28208
hours: Main office Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; call for pharmacy hours
eligibility: North Carolina residents who cannot afford prescription medications. Application and income documentation required.

name: Ada Jenkins Center
description: Food pantry, financial assistance, health services, youth programs, and housing support in the Lake Norman area.
hours: Call for pantry, financial assistance, and program hours
eligibility: Residents of Davidson, Cornelius, and Huntersville. Call to confirm program eligibility and required documents.

name: Mental Health America of Central Carolinas
description: Counseling, support groups, family support, and mental health education for the Charlotte region.
hours: Counseling center Mon-Thu, 9:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Support groups and counseling for people affected by mental illness and their families. Call for intake.
source: Mental Health America of Central Carolinas website

name: Food Bank of Central & Eastern North Carolina
description: Regional food bank serving nine counties from its Raleigh distribution center through partner pantries and meal programs.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Food assistance is provided through partner food pantries. Use the online locator or call for a referral.
source: Food Bank of Central & Eastern North Carolina website

name: Inter-Faith Food Shuttle
description: Food rescue, mobile markets, community gardens, and culinary job training across the Triangle.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Food programs serve Wake and surrounding counties. Call the Food Helpline for distribution sites.

name: Urban Ministries of Wake County
description: Food pantry, free clinic and pharmacy, and emergency shelter for low-income Wake County residents.
hours: Clinic Mon-Thu; call for food pantry and shelter intake hours
eligibility: Low-income Wake County residents. Call for pantry, clinic, and shelter intake requirements.
source: Urban Ministries of Wake County website

name: InterAct of Wake County
description: Free, confidential crisis support, safety planning, counseling, and advocacy for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.
hours: 24-hour crisis line; walk-in Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: Free and confidential services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in Wake County.

name: Durham Rescue Mission
description: Emergency shelter, meals, clothing, recovery programs, and job readiness services for people experiencing homelessness.
hours: Open 24/7
eligibility: Men, women, and children experiencing homelessness. Photo ID and intake screening required.

name: Housing for New Hope
description: Street outreach, housing placement, and supportive services for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Durham.
address: 18 West Colony Place, Suite 250, Durham, NC 27705
hours: Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Durham. Call for outreach and housing program eligibility.

name: Greensboro Urban Ministry
description: Food pantry, emergency shelter, financial assistance, and housing programs for Guilford County neighbors.
address: 305 West Gate City Boulevard, Greensboro, NC 27406
hours: Call for food, shelter, and financial assistance hours
eligibility: Guilford County residents. Call for food, financial, and shelter assistance requirements.

name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Northwest NC
description: Food bank distributing groceries and meals through partner agencies in 18 northwest North Carolina counties.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; call to confirm
eligibility: Food assistance is provided through partner agencies in 18 northwest NC counties. Call for a referral.
source: Second Harvest Food Bank of Northwest NC website

name: ABCCM
description: Crisis assistance, shelter, housing, and medical care for people in need across Buncombe County.
hours: Crisis Ministry Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-4:30 PM; Medical Ministry Mon-Thu
eligibility: People in Buncombe County needing crisis assistance. Veterans, women, and families have specialized housing programs.

name: MANNA FoodBank
description: Western North Carolina's food bank, supplying food and resources to partner pantries across 16 counties.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; Food Helpline Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Food assistance through partner agencies in 16 western NC counties. Call or text the Food Helpline.

name: Good Shepherd Center
description: Meals, emergency shelter, and housing programs for people experiencing homelessness in the Wilmington area.
hours: Call for shelter intake and meal times
eligibility: Adults and families experiencing homelessness or food insecurity in the Wilmington area. Call for intake.

name: Fayetteville Urban Ministry
description: Food pantry, financial assistance, clothing, and youth enrichment programs for Cumberland County residents.
hours: Mon-Thu, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Fri, 9:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Low-income Cumberland County residents. Call for food, financial, and youth program eligibility.

name: Wheels4Hope
description: Repairs and provides reliable vehicles to economically challenged families and individuals referred by partner agencies.
hours: Call for vehicle application and donation hours
eligibility: Low-income individuals and families referred by partner agencies. Vehicle application and eligibility review required.

name: Easterseals PORT Health
description: Disability, mental health, and substance use services for children, adults, and families across North Carolina.
hours: Call for intake and service hours
eligibility: People with disabilities, mental health needs, or substance use challenges. Call for intake and insurance information.

name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope
description: Emergency shelter for women, children, and families with daily meals, case management, health care, and housing-focused support in Charlotte.
hours: Shelter open 24/7; call for intake and coordinated entry hours
eligibility: Women, children, and families experiencing homelessness in Mecklenburg County. Call for shelter assessment and availability.
source: The Salvation Army of Greater Charlotte website

name: Care Ring
description: Low-cost primary care, chronic disease support, and care coordination for uninsured and underinsured Charlotte residents.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed 12:00-1:00 PM
eligibility: Appointment required. Serves uninsured, underinsured, and people who lack access to affordable care; call to schedule.

name: Legal Aid of North Carolina - Charlotte
description: Free civil legal help for low-income residents with housing, benefits, family, consumer, and other legal issues.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: Low-income residents in the Charlotte service area. Call the intake line or visit to request help; not a walk-in emergency service.
source: Legal Aid of North Carolina website

name: Classroom Central
description: Free school supplies and classroom materials for teachers serving high-poverty schools in the Charlotte region.
hours: Mon-Thu, 8:00 AM-6:00 PM; closed Friday
eligibility: Eligible teachers at partner schools in the Charlotte region; register online and shop by appointment.

name: YWCA Central Carolinas
description: Transitional housing for women and families, plus after-school literacy programs, case management, and financial coaching.
hours: Mon-Thu, 7:00 AM-9:00 PM; Fri, 7:00 AM-8:00 PM; Sat-Sun, 8:00 AM-8:00 PM
eligibility: Housing programs are referral-based and not emergency shelter; call 980-283-2334 for Women In Transition or 704-525-5771 for Families Together.

name: American Red Cross - Charlotte Metro Chapter
description: Disaster relief, emergency shelter, food, and recovery support for Mecklenburg and Iredell counties.
hours: 24/7 disaster assistance through 1-800-733-2767; office Mon-Fri
eligibility: Anyone affected by a disaster, including home fires; call the 24-hour Red Cross line for immediate help.

name: Raleigh Rescue Mission
description: Emergency shelter and recovery programs for men in downtown Raleigh and for women and children at its Knightdale campus.
hours: Shelter and intake hours vary by campus; call for current availability
eligibility: Adults and families experiencing homelessness. Call the men's program at 919-508-6212 or the women's program at 919-867-6238.

name: Healing Transitions
description: Residential recovery, detox, and transitional housing for adults experiencing substance use and homelessness in Wake County.
hours: 24/7 residential program; call for intake
eligibility: Adults seeking recovery from substance use. Call for intake; separate men's and women's campuses.

name: Alliance Medical Ministry
description: Primary care, counseling, and wellness services for working uninsured adults in Wake County.
hours: Mon-Wed, 8:15 AM-4:00 PM; Thu, 8:15 AM-12:00 PM and 2:45-4:00 PM; Fri, 8:15 AM-4:00 PM; Sat by appointment
eligibility: Working uninsured adults ages 18+ in Wake County. Appointment required; call 919-250-3320.

name: StepUp Ministry
description: Job training, life skills, financial coaching, and employment placement for adults and young adults in Wake County.
hours: Mon-Thu, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; Fri, 8:30 AM-2:30 PM
eligibility: Adults and young adults in Wake County seeking employment and financial stability; call or attend an information session.

name: Oak City Cares
description: Day resource center offering showers, laundry, meals, phones, computers, and coordinated connections to housing and health services.
hours: Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; Sat-Sun, 9:00 AM-6:00 PM for weekend meals
eligibility: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Wake County. Walk-in services; call for care coordination.

name: Urban Ministries of Durham
description: Emergency shelter, three daily meals, food pantry, clothing closet, and housing-focused case management in Durham.
hours: Shelter front desk open 24/7; call for pantry, closet, and intake hours
eligibility: People experiencing homelessness or poverty in Durham. Shelter intake through Entry Point Durham at 984-287-8313.

name: Durham Crisis Response Center
description: Crisis intervention, emergency shelter, counseling, legal advocacy, and support groups for survivors of domestic and sexual violence.
hours: Office Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; 24-hour help line
eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, family violence, or human trafficking. Call the 24-hour help line for shelter and advocacy.

name: TROSA
description: Long-term residential substance use recovery, vocational training, education, and housing support for adults.
hours: Call admissions for intake and interview scheduling
eligibility: Adults seeking substance use treatment. No referral required; call admissions at 919-419-1059.

name: Lincoln Community Health Center
description: Federally qualified health center providing primary care, pediatrics, behavioral health, and related services in Durham.
hours: Mon-Thu, 8:00 AM-8:00 PM; Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Sat, 8:00 AM-12:00 PM
eligibility: Patients of all ages in Durham; appointments at 919-956-4034. Sliding-fee and insurance assistance available.

name: Families Moving Forward
description: Emergency shelter and case management for families with children experiencing homelessness, plus after-school and enrichment programs.
hours: Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-6:00 PM; after-hours visits by appointment
eligibility: Families with children experiencing homelessness. Complete intake through Entry Point Durham at 984-287-8313 for referral.

name: Interactive Resource Center
description: Day resource center with showers, laundry, computers, mail, a medical clinic, and connections to housing and social services.
hours: Mon-Fri, services 8:00 AM-3:00 PM; offices 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: People experiencing homelessness in Greensboro. Walk-in services; call for specific program availability.

name: Out of the Garden Project
description: Mobile markets, school pantries, and food distribution programs working to reduce childhood hunger in Guilford County.
hours: Office Mon-Thu, 9:00 AM-3:00 PM by appointment; warehouse and market hours vary
eligibility: Children and families facing food insecurity in Guilford County. Check the mobile market schedule or call for site details.
source: Out of the Garden Project website

name: Family Service of the Piedmont
description: Counseling, domestic violence and sexual assault services, financial stability programs, and family support in Guilford County.
hours: Mon-Thu, 8:00 AM-8:00 PM; Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; walk-ins 8:30 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00-2:30 PM
eligibility: Individuals and families in Guilford County. Call the 24/7 crisis line at 336-273-7273 for domestic violence or sexual assault.
source: Family Service of the Piedmont website

name: Samaritan Ministries
description: Soup kitchen, emergency shelter, and housing support serving Winston-Salem and Forsyth County 365 days a year.
hours: Soup kitchen daily; shelter check-in 6:00-7:00 PM; office Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: People experiencing hunger or homelessness in Forsyth County. Call or visit for meal and shelter access.

name: Crisis Control Ministry
description: Emergency rent, utility, food, and prescription assistance with case management for Forsyth County residents.
hours: Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00-4:00 PM
eligibility: Forsyth County residents facing a financial crisis. Call client services for a phone or in-person interview.

name: Winston-Salem Rescue Mission
description: Emergency shelter, meals, recovery programs, and residential support for people experiencing homelessness.
hours: Call for intake and program hours; emergency services available
eligibility: People experiencing homelessness or addiction in Winston-Salem. Call to ask about men's program applications and shelter availability.

name: Homeward Bound of Western North Carolina
description: Day center, street outreach, rapid rehousing, permanent supportive housing, and homelessness prevention in Buncombe County.
hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, 8:00 AM-1:00 PM; Wed, 8:00 AM-11:00 AM
eligibility: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Buncombe County. Visit AHOPE Day Center or call for housing program screening.

name: Western Carolina Rescue Ministries
description: Emergency shelter, meals, recovery programs, and residential support for people experiencing homelessness and addiction.
hours: Office Mon-Fri, 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; emergency services available 24/7
eligibility: People experiencing homelessness or crisis in Asheville. Call for shelter intake and program availability.

name: Pisgah Legal Services
description: Free civil legal aid for low-income residents in Western North Carolina, including housing, benefits, family safety, and consumer issues.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM
eligibility: Low-income residents of Western North Carolina. Every client is screened by phone; apply online or call.

name: Domestic Violence Shelter and Services
description: Emergency shelter, crisis intervention, advocacy, counseling, and support groups for survivors of domestic violence.
hours: 24-hour crisis line; Open Gate office Mon-Fri
eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence and their children in the Wilmington area. Shelter location is confidential; call the 24-hour line.
source: Domestic Violence Shelter and Services website

name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Southeast North Carolina
description: Regional food bank distributing groceries through partner agencies across seven southeastern North Carolina counties.
hours: Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-4:00 PM
eligibility: Food is distributed through partner pantries and meal programs; use the online pantry finder or call for a referral.
source: Second Harvest Food Bank of Southeast North Carolina website
